name: Giliastrum

project_scope.source: Live Master Plant Pool + Polemoniaceae family module; 2026-10-11
project_scope.selection_note: Two approved source-pool concepts. Genus comparison only; not a species installation or native-range reassessment.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Look at a complete flowering shoot and a LOWER leaf together: relatively small, 5-lobed, fused-corolla flowers on peduncles plus alternate, deeply cut lower foliage. Confirm the Polemoniaceae 5-stamen/3-part capsule plan if reproductive material permits.
characters: Herbaceous plants with deeply incised/dissected lower leaves and much narrower upper leaves.
Five spreading corolla lobes joined basally; five stamens and a protruding style in described flowering material.
Capsule and calyx anatomy should be checked rather than assumed from flower color.
shared_genus_recognition.family_door: Phlox usually has simpler, mostly opposite leaves; Ipomopsis rubra has a much longer narrow corolla tube and a tall flowering axis. These are source-pool look-alikes, not interchangeable genus labels.

species_comparison_matrix.Giliastrum rigidulum: About 10–25 cm (4–10 in), commonly low and spreading from the base
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Growing conditions and developmental stage change height; use multiple traits.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Matched full plants with ruler and visible branch origin.

species_comparison_matrix.Giliastrum incisum: Often conspicuously branched in the upper half
species_comparison_matrix.Giliastrum rigidulum: Often many branches spreading from the base
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Damaged or mowed shoots can alter branching.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Entire flowering plant showing base and distal branching.

species_comparison_matrix.caution: Ranges meet near 10 mm; measure multiple fully open flowers in same plane, not buds.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Face-on flowers of both species with millimeter scale.

species_comparison_matrix.Giliastrum incisum: Deep, uneven incisions on mainly lower-stem petiolate leaves; upper leaves become smaller and nearly linear
species_comparison_matrix.Giliastrum rigidulum: Lower leaves irregularly divided into a few oblong, sometimes toothed segments; upper leaves become linear to threadlike
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Both have dissected lower foliage and narrow upper leaves; do not diagnose from a single upper leaf.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Matched basal/lower leaf and upper leaf against neutral background with scale.

species_comparison_matrix.Giliastrum incisum: Hair and gland characters not yet cross-checked against a primary diagnostic key
species_comparison_matrix.Giliastrum rigidulum: Fine glandular hairs described on stems and foliage
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Absence of documented hairs in incisum is NOT evidence of absence. Do not use as binary key.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Matched 10× macro of stem, leaf margin and peduncle.

species_comparison_matrix.Giliastrum incisum: Flowers usually solitary on peduncles about 25–38 mm long
species_comparison_matrix.Giliastrum rigidulum: Flowers on peduncles about 25 mm long
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Length overlaps and is not a safe stand-alone character.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Measured flower peduncles on mature shoots.

field_identification_sequence: 1. Confirm Polemoniaceae: fused five-lobed corolla, five stamens; later check three-part capsule if present.
2. Examine LOWER and UPPER leaves: deeply incised lower foliage grading to narrow upper leaves suggests Giliastrum, not simple-leaved Phlox.
3. View whole plant: erect and chiefly upper-branched suggests G. incisum; short, basally spreading suggests G. rigidulum.
4. Measure several fully open flowers: mostly 6–10 mm favors G. incisum; mostly 10–19 mm favors G. rigidulum.
5. If measurements overlap or the plant is damaged, retain Giliastrum sp. and photograph calyx, stem hairs, leaves, and mature capsule for expert review.
overlap_cautions: At approximately 10 mm, corolla diameters overlap; a single flower does not resolve the pair.
Lower leaves of both species are divided and upper leaves can be threadlike; do not mistake leaf position for species identity.
Flower color is not a reliable separator.
Life-history descriptions vary across secondary sources; do not use annual versus perennial as the primary key.
Descriptions used here are field-guide level; species-level calyx, seed, and capsule characters require primary flora/herbarium verification before being promoted to a definitive key.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.why_confused: Five-lobed fused flowers in the same family
local_source_pool_lookalikes.look_here_first: Mostly opposite, simple leaves and salverform corolla with a conspicuous narrow tube; contrast with alternate, divided lower Giliastrum foliage.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.why_confused: Same family and finely divided foliage
local_source_pool_lookalikes.look_here_first: Very long, slender tubular flowers on a tall flowering axis versus smaller, more open Giliastrum corollas.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.why_confused: Historical names Gilia incisa and Gilia rigidula
local_source_pool_lookalikes.look_here_first: Treat historical names as synonyms/lookup aids, not extra species cards; check accepted-name mapping.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: basal versus upper branching and mature height
diagnostic_photo_checklist.capture: Same scale, include rooted base and highest flowering branch; add 10 cm ruler
At least 3 fully open flowers/species with millimeter ruler; focus on petal tips

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: leaf incision, segment shape, leaf-position gradient
diagnostic_photo_checklist.capture: Lower petiolate leaf plus upper near-linear leaf, label positions and add scale

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: glandular versus nonglandular hairs, pending review
diagnostic_photo_checklist.capture: 10× or better, same lighting; capture stem, leaf surface, peduncle
Flower side view, calyx lobe detail, ripe 3-valved capsule and seeds with scale; do not label species separation until reviewed
One labeled lower-leaf and one flower-side photo per genus, only exact-ID project or licensed sources

handoffs.request: Verify primary flora/herbarium key for calyx-lobe, capsule, seed and glandular-indumentum differences; test corolla diameter ranges (6–10 vs 10–19 mm) and branching descriptions before using as definitive species diagnosis. Do not infer G. incisum is glabrous.
Both source-pool taxa absent from manifest at lesson creation. This genus module does not authorize duplicate or premature canonical cards; installer handles taxonomic identity gate.
Acquire exact-species, provenance-tracked photos only for checklist roles; favor project/user/Joey media when demonstrably exact species, no generic placeholders.
